label: Share of donor program spending above the point of service (management, M&E, supply chain)
source: KFF 2025 (Gaba, Razavi, Kates & Nandakumar, 'Which PEPFAR Investments Drive HIV Outcomes?', Sept 2025; PEPFAR expenditure data, 22 countries, 2018-2023): non-service delivery 'averaged $1.76 billion per year in the 22 countries and accounted for 47% of spending over the period'; it fell by $714M over 2018-2023, so the later share is below the average, and 0.45 is kept. Range 0.30-0.55. (The earlier citation, a PEPFAR 2014 expenditure analysis giving 45%, could not be verified: logic review L-26)

label: ART: multiplier on the country site-level cost (uncertainty)
source: Batch 3+4 (IMP-03). Site-level ART cost per patient-year by country (country_inputs.csv art_site_cost, 2023 US$): the country's median over eligible GHCC Unit Cost Study Repository records (per person per year, provider perspective, no above-service costs, price year 2015 or later, economic x 0.981 financial/economic ratio from Value TB) pooled with the Rosen et al. 2021 (Gates Open Research 5:177) site costs; 7 countries have their own value (Kenya 354, Uganda 371, Malawi 151, Eswatini 255, Zimbabwe 220, Lesotho 148, Zambia 141), South Africa's own median (687) is outside the US$50-600 gate, the other 63 use the median of those countries in their WHO region (AFR 220) or income group. Range = the median across countries of the country range (25th-75th percentile of records, or +/-25% with fewer than 3) relative to its central. audit/batch34_art_costs.py; audit/logic_review/batch34_evidence.md D

label: Elasticity of non-drug (staff) costs to GDP per capita
source: Assumption: salaries rise with income while drugs are priced globally; only applied where no country study exists

label: PMTCT per HIV+ pregnant woman per year under Option B+ (including her ART)
source: Health Policy and Planning 2016;31(8):1133 review of Option B+ cost-effectiveness analyses: annual cost per woman Gopalappa $114 [2011], Ishikawa $170, Ciaranello $179 [2008], Fasawe $194 [2010], Kuznik $470 [2011]; median ~$250 in 2023 US$ (CPI-U). Includes her ART, testing, infant prophylaxis and infant diagnosis. ARV prices have since fallen, so this is conservative.

label: Prevention: cost per HIV infection averted at incidence 1/1000
source: Assumption; scaled by (1/incidence)^0.5. Affects new infections only, not deaths

label: OVC support per child-year (reported only)
source: Assumption; no mortality effect modelled

label: TB: multiplier on income-group cost per patient (uncertainty)
source: Provider cost per patient treated by World Bank income group: Laurence, Griffiths & Vassall 2015 (PharmacoEconomics) systematic review, inflated to 2023 US$ (see unit_cost_reference.csv)

label: Bednets per person-year of net use
source: GiveWell ITN analysis: US$4-6 per net delivered, 1.8 people per net, ~2 years of protection, ~63% of nets used

label: Indoor spraying per person-year protected
source: PMI Africa IRS project, Mali 2012-14: US$6.08-7.40 per person covered (2014 US$), inflated x1.287 (Malaria Journal 2018, s12936-017-2168-2)

label: Malaria case management per case treated (diagnosis + treatment)
source: White et al. 2011, Malaria Journal 10:337 (systematic review of malaria control costs): median financial cost per uncomplicated case treated US$5.84 (range 2.36-23.65) + diagnosis US$4.32 (0.34-9.34), 2009 US$, x1.42 (US CPI-U 2009 to 2023) = about US$14. Low and high add the low and high ends of White et al.'s separate treatment and diagnosis ranges, inflated x1.42; deliberately wide. ACT and RDT prices have fallen since, so current costs may be lower

label: Full cost per child immunized (vaccines + delivery)
source: Delivery: Lydon et al. 2014 (Bull WHO 92:382) non-vaccine health-system cost per infant 2016-20 = US$32.6 (2010 US$) = $45.6 in 2023 US$. Vaccines: MSF The Right Shot 2015, price to fully vaccinate a child in the poorest countries US$32.09-45.59 (2014 US$) = $41.3-58.7 in 2023 US$. Central = delivery + low vaccine price ($87); high = delivery + high price ($104); low = Brenzel 2015 (Vaccine) full cost per DTP3-vaccinated child from Gavi-country cMYPs, US$27 (2010 US$) = $38 (older, cheaper schedules). Check: donor vaccine aid per immunized child in 2021-23 has a median of $40, so donors fund part of the full cost in most countries

label: Excess deaths after stopping ART (multiplier on 1.3/2.5/3.7/4.9/6.0% per yr in years 1-5 and 6.8/7.2/7.3/7.1/6.7% in years 6-10 since stopping)
source: Batch 2 (logic review L-01). CD4-stage cohort calculation (audit/batch2_cohort.py): people who stop ART start in the CD4 distribution of people on ART (ZIMPHIA 2020 Table 10.1, p. 89: median 528 cells/uL, Q1 366, Q3 706; men 411 (282, 558), women 603 (437, 768)), progress at untreated rates (Optima HIV, ten Brink et al. 2025 Lancet HIV appendix Table A1, p. 2: 0.95, 3.00, 3.74, 1.50 years per stage) and die at untreated stage death rates (Table A2, p. 3: 0.36%, 0.58%, 0.88%, 5.9%, 32% a year), minus deaths on suppressive ART (23% of untreated, Table A2). 5-year excess 18.4% (was 17.3%). Range 0.65-1.7 = women + Optima low rates (12.0%) to men + Optima high rates (31.7%). Checks: Brinkhof 2009 (40% of traced patients lost to follow-up had died, 2000-07 cohorts), Zurcher 2017 (24% by 2011), Kaplan 2017 (3% in 17 months, Khayelitsha 2013-14). Applied to full-cost equivalents, each treated as a person who stops ART (Option A)

label: Legacy: new HIV infections per person-year off ART, one value for every country (used only when hiv_legacy_art_params = 1)
source: Pre-Batch-2 value, kept as a sensitivity check. It was set from UNAIDS 6.6M and Optima 4.4-10.7M extra infections over 5 yrs for 20.6M people at PEPFAR-supported sites, a different population from the full-cost equivalents it was applied to (logic review L-41). Replaced by the country's UNAIDS rate x art_transmission_mult

label: Mother-to-child transmission averted by PMTCT
source: WHO AFRO: transmission 15-45% without intervention, below 5% with effective interventions

label: Death by age 2 among infants infected
source: Newell et al. 2004 (Lancet) pooled analysis: 35.2% dead by age 1, 52.5% by age 2 without ART; central lowered for today's infant ART access

label: TB case fatality untreated (HIV-negative)
source: WHO TB burden estimation methods (Glaziou et al.), Table 4

label: TB case fatality treated (HIV-negative)
source: WHO TB burden estimation methods, Table 4

label: TB case fatality untreated (HIV-positive, off ART; blended with the on-ART value by ART coverage)
source: WHO TB burden estimation methods (Glaziou et al.), Table 5, p. 28: ART off, TB treatment off '0.78 (0.65-0.94)'. Blended as 0.78 (1 - ART coverage) + 0.49 x ART coverage (logic review L-13)

label: TB case fatality treated (HIV-positive)
source: WHO TB burden methods, Table 5: 0.09 no ART, 0.04-0.06 on ART

label: Drug-resistant TB: deaths averted per patient treated
source: Assumption: ~60% untreated vs ~15% treated case fatality

label: Bednets/spraying: reduction in malaria deaths at full coverage
source: Eisele, Larsen & Steketee 2010 (Int J Epidemiol, Lives Saved Tool): 55% (49-61%); low end allows for insecticide resistance (GiveWell 40-55%). Child effect size (1-59 months): applied in full to under-5 deaths, scaled by mal_adult_effect_frac for deaths at age 5+

label: Case management: reduction in malaria deaths at full coverage
source: Thwing, Eisele & Steketee 2011, BMC Public Health 11(Suppl 3):S14 (Lives Saved Tool), abstract, Results: protective efficacy of ACT treatment of uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria on malaria mortality '97% (range: 86-99%)' in children 24-59 months and '99% (range: 94-100%)' in children 1-23 months; central = the more conservative 97%. Low = 82% (63-94%), the effect of effective case management of severe malaria (same paper), so the range covers both. Applied in full to under-5 deaths; scaled by mal_adult_effect_frac for deaths at age 5+

label: Bednet use when no survey data
source: Assumption

label: Malaria treatment coverage when no survey data
source: Assumption

label: Future deaths averted per child immunized at U5MR 50
source: Gavi: 20.6M future deaths averted / 1.2B children since 2000 (0.017); 1.7M / 72M in 2024 (0.024)

label: Share of those deaths that would occur within 5 years (before age 5)
source: Li et al. 2021 (Lancet, VIMC): of birth-cohort deaths averted, 38M are hepatitis B (adult deaths) vs 58M measles; adult-onset hepatitis B and HPV deaths fall outside a 5-year window

label: Share of lost HIV testing-and-care money counted as lost ART (the rest has no modelled service effect)
source: Assumption (audit I-09). Testing and care money (IHME care and support, counselling and testing) funds diagnosis, linkage and retention; half of a loss is counted as people-equivalents who stop ART at the full ART cost. Batch 3+4 (L-05): this parameter no longer applies to systems money (see hss_service_share); a flow-of-initiations treatment (IMP-02c) is blocked for lack of a cost per initiation (audit/logic_review/batch34_evidence.md, C)

label: Share of people losing donor-funded services who keep them anyway
source: Assumption: some patients are absorbed by government facilities or cheaper delivery without new money

label: TB spread: secondary active TB cases caused per untreated TB patient (conservative: one year of infectiousness)
source: Derived: an untreated smear-positive case infects about 10 people a year (Styblo 1991, Bull Int Union Tuberc Lung Dis); about 60% of pulmonary TB is smear-positive (WHO); 5-10% of the newly infected develop active TB, most within 2-5 years (Vynnycky & Fine 1997, Epidemiol Infect). 10 x 0.6 x ~0.07 = ~0.4. New cases appear 1-2 years later and are treated at the reduced coverage

label: Malaria rebound: yearly growth in the extra deaths from lost vector control while the loss lasts
source: Assumption on size, direction from Cohen et al. 2012 (Malaria Journal 11:122): 75 malaria resurgence events in 61 countries, 1930s-2000s, most linked to weakened control programs (funding, supply interruptions)

label: Chance of eventually dying of HIV after infection without treatment
source: Todd et al. 2007 (AIDS 21 Suppl 6) and CASCADE: median survival about 11 years from HIV infection without antiretroviral therapy; most untreated people die of HIV within 20 years

label: Chance of eventually dying of HIV after infection with treatment
source: Assumption: people diagnosed and kept on ART have near-normal life expectancy; this allows for late diagnosis and treatment interruptions

label: Median survival after HIV infection without treatment
source: Todd et al. 2007 (AIDS 21 Suppl 6, ALPHA network, African cohorts): Weibull survival with median about 10.5 years for people infected at age 25-34 (12.5 at 15-24, 8.6 at 35-44); shape 2.25 as in UNAIDS Spectrum. Sets when deaths from new infections occur, so how many fall by 2035

label: Share of people still off ART at the end of 2030 who return to care each year once funding is back
source: Batch 2 (indirect evidence: individual disengagement while services ran, not a programme restart). Kranzer et al. 2010 JAIDS 55:e17: 'The probability of resuming therapy within 3 years of defaulting therapy was 42% (event rate = 21.4 per 100 person-years)' (0.17 a year); Kaplan et al. 2017 PLoS Med 14:e1002407: 'approximately 50% of patients who disengage will return to care by 2.5 years' (about 0.3 a year); Mody et al. 2026 PLoS Med 23:e1005052 (Zambia, >30 days late): return by 12 months 67.7% in control clinics (0.68). Central 0.35, range 0.17-0.68. Until they return they keep the excess death risk by years since stopping (years 6-10 after 2030)

label: Malaria: effect at age 5+ as a share of the child (1-59 months) effect sizes
source: Assumption: no published adult LiST effect found; child effect scaled. The Lives Saved Tool effects (mal_vc_eff, mal_cm_eff) are for children 1-59 months; under-5 share of each country's malaria deaths from WHO/MCEE child deaths / WHO all-age deaths (0.76 SSA / 0.40 elsewhere if missing)

label: TB case fatality untreated (HIV-positive, on ART for a year or more)
source: WHO TB burden estimation methods (Glaziou et al.), Table 5, p. 28: ART >= 1 year, TB treatment off '0.49 (0.31-0.70)' (source: assumptions, per the table)

label: Malaria: share of malaria deaths in children under 5, WHO African Region
source: WHO World Malaria Report 2025, section 2.3 (WHO African Region), p. 20: 'Just over 75% of all deaths in the region are of children aged under 5 years.' Range +/-5 points: assumption around the WHO point estimate

label: Malaria: share of malaria deaths in children under 5, WHO Region of the Americas
source: WHO World Malaria Report 2025, section 2.4 (Americas), p. 24: 'Children aged under 5 years accounted for less than 25% of all deaths in the region.' WHO gives only an upper bound, so central 0.20 and range 0.15-0.25 (assumption within WHO's bound)

label: Malaria: share of malaria deaths in children under 5, WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region
source: WHO World Malaria Report 2025, section 2.5 (Eastern Mediterranean), p. 28: 'Children aged under 5 years accounted for 36.4% of all deaths.' Range +/-5 points: assumption around the WHO point estimate

label: Malaria: share of malaria deaths in children under 5, WHO South-East Asia Region
source: WHO World Malaria Report 2025, section 2.7 (South-East Asia), pp. 31-32: 'Just under a quarter of all malaria deaths in the region were in children aged under 5 years.' Range +/-5 points: assumption around the WHO point estimate

label: Malaria: share of malaria deaths in children under 5, WHO Western Pacific Region
source: WHO World Malaria Report 2025, section 2.8 (Western Pacific), p. 35: 'Children aged under 5 years accounted for 40.0% of all deaths in the region.' Range +/-5 points: assumption around the WHO point estimate

label: Malaria: sensitivity switch, 1 = use the country child-death series for the under-5 share (default 0 = off)
source: Sensitivity check only. 1 = the previous rule (WHO/MCEE child malaria deaths 2021 / WHO all-age deaths 2024, clipped 0-1), which mixes two estimation methods and years (logic review IMP-05 follow-up). Default 0: the World Malaria Report 2025 regional share

label: Multiplier on the country's HIV transmission rate per person with unsuppressed viral load (UNAIDS 2025 new infections / (PLHIV - suppressed), country_inputs.csv art_transmission_rate)
source: Batch 2 (logic review L-41). The country rate is UNAIDS AIDSinfo 2026 estimates (2025): New HIV Infections (all ages) / (People living with HIV - People living with HIV who have suppressed viral loads), unrounded; a person who stops ART becomes a person with unsuppressed viral load. Dashboard countries: median 0.12, IQR 0.085-0.131 (Kenya 0.070, Nigeria 0.122, Mozambique 0.130, South Africa 0.077, Uganda 0.125); countries without the suppression indicator get their WHO-region median. Range 0.71-1.38 = the median ratio of the UNAIDS lower / upper infection bounds to the estimate. Cross-check: 2.24 linked transmissions per 100 person-years among serodiscordant couples with an untreated partner (Donnell et al. 2010 Lancet 375:2092)

label: Mean years a person newly infected by someone who stopped ART stays unsuppressed and transmits (second-generation infections)
source: Assumption (Batch 2). Median time from infection to diagnosis in sub-Saharan Africa 2.6 years (1.8-3.5) in 2020 (Giguere et al. 2021 Lancet HIV 8:e284, Shiny90), plus linkage and 0.2 years to suppression (Optima appendix Table A2); exponential mean = median / ln 2, about 4 years. Only one further generation is counted

label: Sensitivity switch: 1 = the ART values before Batch 2 (death risk 1.2-5.0% a year, transmission art_transmission for every country, 50% a year return to care, no second generation)
source: Default 0 (off). Keeps the pre-Batch-2 behaviour reproducible as a sensitivity check (logic review L-01, L-41)

label: Share of lost systems money (labs/HR/M&E/supply chain) that still cuts services (structural switch)
source: Assumption (Batch 3+4, logic review L-05, option (ii) of IMP-02). Systems money is above-site money; the unit costs of ART and TB treatment are site costs x 1/(1 - asd_share), which already prices above-site costs into every patient, so converting systems money into patients a second time counted it twice. Central 0 (no conversion). Held constant in the draws like hiv_legacy_art_params: a draw range above a central of 0 is one-sided (every draw converts more money than the central run), which puts the central outside the displayed range; the structural alternative is run as a sensitivity case by setting it to the pre-batch 0.5 (range 0.25-0.9). No study quantifies how much systems money becomes service delivery
